title: MachO-explorer JSON envelope
description:
The single response shape every tool emits under --json, and the shape the MCP server returns in structuredContent. One envelope for every tool and both doors, so a consumer learns it once.

`data` is deliberately unconstrained here. Each tool's own answer shape is a function of the file it read, is documented in the TypeScript declarations (src/api.d.ts), and is the thing most likely to grow; constraining it in one schema would make this file a second, worse copy of those declarations. What this schema pins is the envelope itself — which is the part every consumer must be able to rely on, and the part that has to stay identical across ten tools and two doors.

Addresses inside `data` are hex strings, never JSON numbers: a 64-bit address does not survive one. That is enforced by convention rather than by this schema, because the schema cannot see inside an unconstrained object — the address-bearing types are documented in src/api.d.ts and asserted by test/types.mjs.

schemaVersion.description: Version of the envelope shape, not of the package. Bump the major on a removal, a rename, or a change of meaning; bump the minor when a field is added, since an added field is ignorable. Compare it against the value you were written against and fail loudly on a change, rather than discovering it from an empty field.

tool.description: Which tool produced this. Over MCP this is the tool name with the 'macho-' prefix; from the CLI it is the unprefixed name.

ok.description: True when the tool ran, whether or not it found anything. An empty result is ok:true — 'ran and found nothing' is an answer, not a failure. False means the tool could not do its job.

binary.description: The file that was read, or null when none was named. Over MCP there is no fallback binary, so this is null unless the caller passed one.

errors.description: Machine-readable reason codes, empty when ok is true. These are what let a caller self-correct rather than parse prose: 'io' and 'unknown-encoding' are different problems, and conflating them sends a caller looking in the wrong place.

messages.description: Prose for a human, one per code above. Absent rather than empty when there is nothing to say, which keeps 'nothing to report' distinguishable from 'there is nothing there'.

notes.description: Caveats that do not make the answer wrong — that zero is the correct answer for a stripped binary, that a slice was chosen by preference rather than by request. Absent rather than empty, for the same reason as messages.

data.description: The answer. Null when ok is false. Shape documented per function in src/api.d.ts.

data.note: address is not mapped by this slice — nothing here to resolve

messages: /nope: cannot be read (no such file, not a regular file, or not permitted)
